clue.text: Finally finds places to buy underwear

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word finds

parts.note: shopping malls are places to buy things

explanation.surface: Someone at last tracks down the shops where they can buy their pants.
explanation.definitionFit: Smalls is British slang for underclothes, especially when washed or hung up to dry.

clue.text: Former Tommies bursting with energy

indicators.note: bursting means breaking apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Old soldiers full of vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommies are British soldiers. 'bursting' scrambles TOMMIES plus E.
explanation.definitionFit: Sometime as an adjective means one-time or erstwhile, describing a previous role.

clue.text: Briefly showing clutch and part of carburettor

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: airing means showing, as in airing a programme
to clutch something is to take it

explanation.surface: A brief demonstration of a car's clutch and carburettor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' trims AIRING to AIRIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The air intake is the opening through which a carburettor draws in air to mix with fuel.

clue.text: Dictator's solitary sub

indicators.note: a dictator here is one who dictates, speaking words for someone to write

parts.note: solitary means alone, lone

explanation.surface: A tyrant's lonely submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' reads as tyrant, but signals speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A sub is a small advance or loan of money, as against wages.

clue.text: Georgia's neighbour is lazy worker, according to Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner's name signals that the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: lazy means slack
a worker is a bee, as in a worker bee in a hive

explanation.surface: A slacker employee is supposedly next door to Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Georgia' tempts toward the US state, but this is the country, which borders the sea. SLACK BEE with initial sounds swapped gives BLACK SEA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Black Sea forms the western border of the Caucasus country of Georgia.

clue.text: Afflicted by the runs?

parts.note: the runs seems to mean diarrhoea, but here it is the ladders that run down damaged stockings or tights

explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' suggests an upset stomach, but stockings can suffer runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tights with ladders have lines of unravelled stitches, known in America as runs.

clue.text: Restrained Tory was abusive on line

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, a Tory
an internet troll posts abuse online, so trolled means was abusive on line

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician was held back after abusing people online.
explanation.definitionFit: Controlled behaviour is held in check, restrained.

clue.text: Berks perhaps feeding heroin to father

indicators.note: feeding something to a person puts it into them, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a father
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Idiots giving drugs to their dad.
explanation.walkthrough: Berks is short for Berkshire, an English county; 'berks' as slang means idiots.
explanation.definitionFit: A shire is an English county, of which Berkshire is one example.

clue.text: Hostile to state, subversive's content to drop out

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

indicators.note: the inner letters, the content, drop out of the word, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: A dissident, unwilling to follow the state, drops out of society.
explanation.definitionFit: Averse means opposed or disinclined, as in averse to risk.

clue.text: It's passed on from bachelor to knight

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A title or honour handed down from a single man to a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passed on' suggests inheritance, but it is a relay baton.
explanation.definitionFit: In a relay race the runners pass a short stick from one to the next.

clue.text: Wine stains start to annoy the French

parts.note: to stain or spoil is to mar, so stains means mars

indicators.note: start to points to the opening letter of the word annoy

parts.note: la is a French word for the

explanation.surface: Spilt wine leaves marks that irritate the French.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsala is a fortified wine from Sicily, named after the town where it is made.

clue.text: Antecedent in Essex possesses most of teeth

indicators.note: the phrase possesses the answer within its letters, signalling a hidden word

explanation.surface: An ancestor from Essex has most of a set of teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possesses' tells you the letters run across 'antecedent in Essex'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentine is the hard tissue forming the bulk of a tooth beneath its enamel.

clue.text: Hit reef perhaps, travelling westward

indicators.note: in an across entry, going westward means reading right to left, so the word is turned around

parts.note: a reef knot is one example of a knot

explanation.surface: A ship strikes a reef while sailing west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reef' suggests rocks, but here it is a type of knot.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonk is British slang for strike hard, as in a batter's big shot in cricket.

clue.text: Roughly chop some sorrel

indicators.note: chopping the words up and rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: coarsely chop a bit of sorrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roughly' looks like the manner of chopping but is the definition; 'chop' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean approximately, giving an estimate rather than an exact figure.

clue.text: Remorse of notary oddly accepted by Congress

indicators.note: accepted by means taken inside, so one part sits within the other

parts.note: congress in its old sense means sexual intercourse, coition

indicators.note: oddly means the letters in odd positions of the word notary

explanation.surface: A notary's regret is officially acknowledged by the US legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' looks like the US legislature; it means sexual union.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrition is deep sorrow for wrongdoing, a penitent remorse.

clue.text: Old wife on booze in field

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the old wife comes after the booze

parts.note: mead is an alcoholic drink made from honey
W is the abbreviation for wife, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: An elderly wife drinking in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A meadow is a grassy field, often used for hay.

clue.text: One with no illusions about top celebrities

parts.note: re is a formal word meaning about or concerning
the A-list is the set of most famous celebrities

explanation.surface: A clear-eyed observer who sees through the glamour of famous stars.
explanation.definitionFit: A pragmatist sees things as they are, without fanciful hopes or delusions.

clue.text: Responds to new allegations about delay in parliament

definitions.meaning: how politicians typically react to fresh charges: by obstructing and refusing to answer
to obstruct proceedings in parliament by filibustering

explanation.surface: A politician answers fresh charges about obstruction in the Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is ironic: the typical response is to block questions.
explanation.definitionFit: To stonewall is to block, by evasive non-answers or by long speeches holding up a debate.

clue.text: Dash across part of Scotland, missing last lecture

indicators.note: across means stretched over, so one word is put around the other

parts.note: to dash is to hare, run fast

indicators.note: missing last means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Angus is a council area in eastern Scotland

explanation.surface: Rushing through a Scottish region without stopping to give a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash' looks like a noun but is the verb hare; 'missing last' drops the final S, and 'across' puts the shortened Scottish area (Angus, a council area) inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A harangue is a long, forceful speech, a lecture or tirade.

clue.text: Boxers, for example, answer me roughly

indicators.note: roughly means put together loosely, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fighter roughly demands an answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxers' suggests fighters; they are shorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxer shorts are one kind of clothing sold for men.

clue.text: Philosopher twisted back of thigh

parts.note: something bent is twisted out of shape
the ham is the back of the thigh, as in hamstring

explanation.surface: A thinker who has pulled a hamstring.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeremy Bentham was the English philosopher who founded utilitarianism.

clue.text: Extremely virile conk with prominent blood vessels

indicators.note: extremely points to the two end letters of the word virile

parts.note: conk is British slang for the nose

explanation.surface: A manly nose covered in visible veins.
explanation.definitionFit: Venose is a botanical and anatomical term meaning marked with many veins.

clue.text: Forked out over £50 for pasty!

indicators.note: over here means covering, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to fork out is to pay, so forked out means paid
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone paid over fifty pounds for a Cornish pasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pasty' looks like the pie but is an adjective meaning pale.
explanation.definitionFit: A pallid complexion is pale and unhealthy-looking, like a pasty face.

clue.text: Attempt to influence shy, loveless lad

parts.note: to shy is to throw, and lob means throw

indicators.note: loveless means without O, love in tennis scoring, which is dropped

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: Trying to win over a timid boy who has no love.
explanation.definitionFit: To lobby is to campaign to sway lawmakers or other people in power.

clue.text: Coffees spreading nice aromas

indicators.note: the letters spread about and rearrange

explanation.surface: Cups of coffee give off pleasant smells.
explanation.definitionFit: Americanos are espresso drinks diluted with hot water.

clue.text: The King of the Fairies with onset of idea for drug

indicators.note: for here means in place of, so one letter swaps out

parts.note: elves are small fairy beings
E is slang for ecstasy, a drug

indicators.note: onset of means the opening letter of idea

explanation.surface: Oberon, monarch of the fairy folk, gets an idea about drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The King of the Fairies' looks like one phrase; 'The King' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley is nicknamed the King of Rock and Roll.

clue.text: On the radio, inspirational female sounds catty

indicators.note: broadcasting on the radio means what is heard rather than written

parts.note: a Muse is a goddess who inspires artists

explanation.surface: A broadcast star who inspires others comes across as spiteful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catty' suggests spite, but here it means cat-like noises.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat mews, so mews is making the sounds of a cat.

clue.text: Money for poker upset smoker

indicators.note: upset means turned upside down, read upward in a down entry

parts.note: Etna is a smoking volcano in Sicily

explanation.surface: Losing poker money annoys a smoker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smoker' suggests a person with a cigarette, but it is a volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: An ante is the stake each player puts into the pot before cards are dealt.

clue.text: The imposition of taxes ultimately will cause strife

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letters of the words will and cause

parts.note: strife is contention, and vying is contending with rivals

explanation.surface: A warning that taxation will eventually lead to conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: To levy is to impose a tax, so the levying of taxes is their imposition.

clue.text: Spy regularly argued for restraint

parts.note: James Bond is the fictional spy

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word argued

explanation.surface: A secret agent often pleaded for self-control.
explanation.definitionFit: Bondage is being held in bonds, a state of physical restraint or captivity.

clue.text: Dig up endless dirt about evil leaders of the Earth

indicators.note: about means going around, so the shortened word surrounds the rest
endless means the word dirt loses its final letter

parts.note: evil is sin, wrongdoing

indicators.note: leaders of means the first letters of the words the and Earth

explanation.surface: Excavating soil to unearth wickedness among the planet's rulers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the final T of dirt, and 'about' wraps what remains around the evil and the two leading letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To disinter is to exhume, removing a buried body from the ground.

clue.text: Old copper kitchen utensil

definitions.meaning: a nineteenth-century policeman, named after Sir Robert Peel who founded the force
a tool for removing skin from vegetables and fruit

explanation.surface: An antique copper pan in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' suggests a metal pan; it is a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Peelers and Bobbies were early London police; a peeler also strips potato skin.
